title: GraphFrames joins Spark, Iceberg View Spec Updates, Parquet SERIALIZED_VALUE, and Agent SQL Queries
summary: Co-hosts Scott Haines and Lisa Cao review a busy week across the open data ecosystem, from AI-assisted software development to new project proposals and releases. They discuss how shared specifications and language-neutral tools are changing data engineering, and why good community practices matter in open source.
notesHtml:
Co-hosts Scott Haines and Lisa Cao review a busy week across the open data ecosystem, from AI-assisted software development to new project proposals and releases. They discuss how shared specifications and language-neutral tools are changing data engineering, and why good community practices matter in open source.
  • Scott and Lisa discuss AI code reviews, agent-to-agent workflows, and the risks of reviews that lack project history or expand a pull request beyond its intended scope. They consider whether platforms like GitHub will evolve to better support agents.
  • New Go and TypeScript SDKs for Airflow, alongside developments in Rust, C, and other ecosystems, point toward broader language support and new questions about dependency compatibility.
  • LakeKeeper adds write privileges that separate writing data from destructive operations. DataFusion Distributed, a library for adding distributed execution to existing DataFusion applications, is moving toward subproject status; unlike Ballista, it leaves worker management and deployment to the application.
  • The Iceberg view specification aims to make views portable across query engines. Scott and Lisa also discuss how shared specifications can reduce bespoke integrations and make project requirements easier for both people and AI agents to follow.
  • The hosts cover ALP floating-point encoding, an Arrow extension type for Parquet files, and a proposed Parquet serialized-value logical type for data such as Protobuf and Thrift.
  • GraphFrames is being reintroduced into Spark. A proposal would extend real-time mode to distributed batch SQL and DataFrame queries, with early tests reporting faster performance on several workloads.
  • New Swift and Rust client updates lead to a discussion of running Spark Connect from phones, embedded devices, and potentially browsers through WebAssembly.
  • Congrats to new committers and encourage people to be constructive on developer mailing lists, where discussions and comments remain part of the project record.

title: Apache Spark 4.3, Parquet FINITE Vector, Datafusion Comet 1.2, Nvidia's cuDF, and Airflow 3.4
summary: This week, Scott and Lisa cover one of the busiest release weeks yet across the open lakehouse ecosystem, led by the Apache Spark 4.3.0 release. They also discuss Parquet’s new vector proposal, Iceberg V4 spec votes, catalog security hardening, and big releases from DataFusion Comet, NVIDIA’s cuDF plugin for Spark, and Airflow. Along the way, they talk about giving agents downtime, why security fixes keep landing across projects, and why keeping your stack up to date matters more than ever.
notesHtml:
This week, Scott and Lisa cover one of the busiest release weeks yet across the open lakehouse ecosystem, led by the Apache Spark 4.3.0 release. They also discuss Parquet’s new vector proposal, Iceberg V4 spec votes, catalog security hardening, and big releases from DataFusion Comet, NVIDIA’s cuDF plugin for Spark, and Airflow. Along the way, they talk about giving agents downtime, why security fixes keep landing across projects, and why keeping your stack up to date matters more than ever.

  • Parquet’s FINITE_VECTOR logical type proposal, which uses LIST storage, along with follow-on work in an Iceberg draft spec PR and a Spark SPIP.
  • Lakekeeper 0.15.0, including an OpenFGA write privilege that doesn’t grant drop, cache invalidation, autoscaling task workers, and scoped vended credentials.
  • Unity Catalog’s work toward 0.8.0 with stricter privilege checks and new privileges, plus a Polaris fix for table corruption when a commit’s outcome is unknown.
  • Iceberg V4 votes on default value expressions and stats-only fields, and Iceberg Rust 0.11 with encrypted writes, deletion vectors, and a new catalog auth design.
  • The move of iceberg-datafusion into the DataFusion project starting with 0.12, and what that means for your Cargo.toml.
  • hudi-rs 0.6.0 with experimental merge-on-read metadata table compaction, and Paimon’s Mosaic 0.3.0 for tables with 10,000+ columns.
  • Spark 4.3.0 highlights, including stateful Real-Time Mode, Project Feather for single-node workloads, SCD Type 2 in Spark Declarative Pipelines, new variant functions, nanosecond timestamps (preview), DSv2 updates, and the move to Python 3.11+.
  • Spark proposals, including the passed External Lookup Join SPIP, a new ADBC data source SPIP, DSv2 join pushdown, and future Java version minimums.
  • Flink on Ray (FLIP-608), the Flink Agents preview, and geography type discussions, plus Kafka 4.4.0 and a JWT signature validation fix in 4.3.2.
  • DataFusion Comet 1.2.0, with memory, spill, and shuffle improvements, opt-in native Iceberg v3 writes, Delta Lake scans, Arrow Python UDFs, and official Spark 4.2 support.
  • NVIDIA’s cuDF plugin for Spark (formerly Spark RAPIDS) 26.10, with GPU acceleration for variant, expanded Delta Lake support, and Iceberg v3 deletion vectors.
  • Airflow 3.4.0, with task loops (AIP-111), the Dag Importer for TypeScript, Go, Java, and YAML (AIP-85), metadata database improvements, and hardened Docker images, plus the Common AI provider 1.1.0.
  • Quick mentions of MLflow 3.18 and Omnigent 0.21.

title: AI Special: Mistral's Le Chonk, Agent Standards, GLM-5.3 Evaluation, and More w/ Melanie Warrick
summary: Temporal developer relations engineer Melanie Warrick joins hosts Lisa Cao and Scott Haines to review latest open source model releases and agent orchestration frameworks for the week. The episode covers a wide range of AI news, from Mistral’s massive LeChonk model and GLM-5.3’s cybersecurity evaluation to new standards, inference infrastructure, agent harnesses, and voice-agent tooling. The discussion focuses on how open models, runtime environments, observability, and governance are shaping the next phase of AI development.
notesHtml:
Temporal developer relations engineer Melanie Warrick joins hosts Lisa Cao and Scott Haines to review latest open source model releases and agent orchestration frameworks for the week. The episode covers a wide range of AI news, from Mistral’s massive LeChonk model and GLM-5.3’s cybersecurity evaluation to new standards, inference infrastructure, agent harnesses, and voice-agent tooling. The discussion focuses on how open models, runtime environments, observability, and governance are shaping the next phase of AI development.
  • Mistral’s LeChonk, a trillion-parameter open-weight multimodal model, including its hardware requirements, MIT licensing, gated cyber variant, and potential cybersecurity applications
  • GLM-5.3’s Regular evaluation, including multi-stage cyberattack scenarios, prompt-injection risks, rule-breaking behavior, and questions around model guardrails
  • The Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation additions, including Anthropic’s Agent Skills, OpenAI’s Open Responses, Hugging Face’s reinforcement-learning environments, and Alibaba’s OpenSandbox
  • LLMD’s graduation within the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, including Kubernetes-native distributed inference, vLLM and SGLang support, endpoint picking, high availability, and multi-tenant flow control
  • Hermit, Raven, Google’s Harness, and related agent-harness research focused on tools, memory, retries, checks, modular workflows, and harnesses that can evolve around a model
  • Nano Muse, Deepgram’s acquisition of Daily and PipeCat, GitLab Orbit, NVIDIA OpenShell, Google Cloud’s Agent Compute Engine, and Bubble Agent 2

title: DuckDB 2.0, External Lookup Joins, Arrow Database Connectivity, and OpenCode 2.0
summary: This week, Scott and Lisa recap a busy week across the open lakehouse ecosystem, from DuckDB 2.0 and Iceberg’s evolving V4 spec to new proposals for Spark, Flink, and Airflow. They also discuss catalog security and project governance, plus updates to Apache Comet, OpenCode, and Omnigent. Together, they highlight the latest developments, security fixes, and community changes shaping the open-source data landscape.
notesHtml:
This week, Scott and Lisa recap a busy week across the open lakehouse ecosystem, from DuckDB 2.0 and Iceberg’s evolving V4 spec to new proposals for Spark, Flink, and Airflow. They also discuss catalog security and project governance, plus updates to Apache Comet, OpenCode, and Omnigent. Together, they highlight the latest developments, security fixes, and community changes shaping the open-source data landscape.

  • DuckDB 2.0 and DuckLake 1.1, including new lakehouse features, the Quack client-server protocol, asynchronous I/O, and breaking changes to plan for when upgrading.
  • Unity Catalog and Lakekeeper changes, including stricter privilege checks, distributed cache invalidation, and updates to credential handling.
  • Paimon’s new Terraform/OpenTofu provider for managing tables, roles, and policies as code.
  • Iceberg V4 discussions around file types, multimodal data, efficient column updates, single-file commits, and metadata overhead from small writes.
  • An Arrow security fix for a vulnerability involving KMS URLs embedded in encrypted Parquet files, with a recommendation to upgrade to Arrow 26.0.0.
  • Apache DataFusion Comet’s top-level project proposal, including its growing contributor community and a proposed limit on concurrent open pull requests.
  • StreamFusion’s possible move toward becoming a Flink subproject and what shifting project ownership can mean for users and contributors.
  • Spark proposals for ADBC connectivity and external lookup joins, including early prototype benchmarks showing 3–10x read throughput over JDBC on column-oriented databases.
  • Airflow’s inbound webhook proposal and how webhooks could support event-triggered workflows.
  • OpenCode 2.0’s background agents, execution modes, and plugin support, along with Omnigent 0.19.0 and 0.19.1 updates.
  • New Paimon, Flink, and Arrow committers, along with a new Iceberg PMC member.

title: Unity Catalog 0.7, Paimon 2.1, Hudi 1.1.2, Arrow 26.0, and new ASF top-level projects
summary: Scott Haines and Lisa Cao are back after a flu-delayed skip, just in time for Week 42 — which, yes, is our favorite week - "Hitchhiker’s Guide" week. We tear through a stacked open lakehouse release week, led by Unity Catalog 0.7.0, shipping native Iceberg REST catalog support, with Paimon, Hudi, Arrow, MLflow, and OmniGent close behind.
notesHtml:
Scott Haines and Lisa Cao are back after a flu-delayed skip, just in time for Week 42 — which, yes, is our favorite week - "Hitchhiker’s Guide" week. We tear through a stacked open lakehouse release week, led by Unity Catalog 0.7.0, shipping native Iceberg REST catalog support, with Paimon, Hudi, Arrow, MLflow, and OmniGent close behind.

In this episode

  • Cold open / Week 42. Scott had the flu, last week vanished into the void, and the “answer to life, the universe, and the open lakehouse” ...
  • Unity Catalog 0.7.0. Native Iceberg REST catalog support, plus a playground so you can try classic Unity Catalog and the new Iceberg path without assembling a lab from spare parts.
  • Production hardening. Live, ready, and metrics endpoints; multi-instance setups behind a load balancer; Spark support through 4.1, with 4.2 still waiting on upstream Iceberg.
  • Apache Paimon 2.1.0. Multimodal and table-format upgrades: scan planning, Arrow reads/writes, blob collections, variant updates, indexes, and full-text search.
  • Iceberg compatibility, no shortcuts. Paimon stays aligned with Iceberg’s published type model — including the fussy bits, like nanosecond timestamps and variant.
  • Apache Hudi 1.1.2. Stronger Apache Flink streaming merge-on-read, 19 backported fixes, and a Flink upsert bug fix that keeps writes from quietly going missing.
  • Apache Kafka 4.2.2. A short stop: mostly a performance-oriented release.
  • Apache Arrow 26.0.0. The vote passed, the release is official, and Jeffrey Vo joins the PMC.
  • MLflow 3.17.1 and 3.17.2. Decision API support, custom judges, evaluation lineage, and UI fixes for Claude Code OpenTelemetry traces.
  • OmniGent 0.18. Bring-your-own-agents, web reading that turns pages into clean markdown, plus GitLab MR and Azure DevOps PR integrations.

Community, the Apache Way, and how not to land a 4,000-line first PR

The back half leaves the changelog and talks about project health: incubator graduation, contributor onboarding, CI cost, release management, and why credibility in a community still beats dropping a giant patch on day one.

Lisa also flags three new ASF top-level projects:

  • Apache Auron — a native, Rust-powered accelerator for big data query engines
  • Apache Reqsign — a lightweight signer for cloud storage HTTP requests, without hauling around vendor SDKs
  • Apache ResilientDB — a modular, permissioned blockchain framework built on Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus

title: Nanosecond Timestamp Precision, Iceberg-Datafusion,Spark Connect Rust Client, and Parquet Types
summary: The biggest throughline this week is format-layer consolidation. Apache Parquet 2.14.0 shipped as a final release, carrying chronological ordering for INT96 timestamps and Variant documentation fixes, while a parallel dev-list debate over versioning semantics and reader behavior for unsupported versions shows the community is actively thinking about long-term compatibility contracts, not just feature additions.
notesHtml:
The biggest throughline this week is format-layer consolidation. Apache Parquet 2.14.0 shipped as a final release, carrying chronological ordering for INT96 timestamps and Variant documentation fixes, while a parallel dev-list debate over versioning semantics and reader behavior for unsupported versions shows the community is actively thinking about long-term compatibility contracts, not just feature additions.

One layer up, Lance v12 is in a sustained beta sprint, shipping six beta releases in a single week. The work spans file format stabilization (resolving the stable format to 2.2), distributed vector search in Java, in-memory WAL improvements, and IVF index optimization. This is not routine maintenance; it reads as a deliberate push to lock down a production-ready v12 surface before a GA cut.

At the query engine and integration layer, two parallel votes to move iceberg-rust's DataFusion integration into the Apache DataFusion project are the most structurally interesting governance event of the week. If both votes pass, Iceberg catalog access becomes a first-class DataFusion concern rather than a satellite project, which changes how engine builders think about Iceberg adoption. Separately, the Spark Connect Rust client reached RC2 for its 4.2.0 release, and Spark 4.3.0 RC1 is in vote, keeping the Spark release cadence unusually active.
